quests.instruction: You hear a strange creaking noise under your bed. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Odd sounds you cannot explain can make your heart beat a little faster.
quests.explanation: Strange sounds you cannot explain can give your heart a nervous flutter.
quests.funFact: Houses creak because wood changes a tiny bit with temperature — it is not magic!

quests.instruction: Your balloon slips out of your hand and floats away. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Watching something float away that you wanted to keep can bring a little frown.
quests.explanation: Watching something you loved float away can bring a quiet, disappointed feeling.
quests.funFact: Balloons float because the gas inside is lighter than the air around us!

quests.instruction: Someone breaks your favorite crayon on purpose. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: When someone damages something you love on purpose, your face might get hot.
quests.explanation: It is upsetting when someone breaks something you care about on purpose.
quests.funFact: Most broken crayons can still be used — they just look a little different!

quests.instruction: It is officially the first day of summer break! How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: The start of a long, fun break can make you want to cheer out loud.
quests.explanation: The start of a long break full of possibilities feels thrilling.
quests.funFact: Many children make a summer wish list to plan all their fun activities!

quests.instruction: Grandma bakes your favorite cookies. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: The smell of warm cookies can make you feel cozy and glad.
quests.explanation: Warm cookies made just for you are a happy little surprise.
quests.funFact: The smell of baking can make people feel happy even before the first bite!

quests.instruction: Loud fireworks boom and crackle outside your window. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Sudden loud bangs can make your shoulders jump up.
quests.explanation: Sudden, loud bangs can make your body jump and your heart beat fast.
quests.funFact: Gently covering your ears can help loud firework sounds feel less overwhelming.

quests.instruction: You leave your library book behind at the park. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Realizing you lost something you were enjoying can make your face droop.
quests.explanation: Losing something you were enjoying, like a good book, can feel disappointing.
quests.funFact: Most libraries are happy to help if a book gets lost — just ask a grown-up!

quests.instruction: Your brother eats the last cookie you were saving. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: Losing a treat you were saving for later does not feel fair.
quests.explanation: Losing something special you were saving can feel very unfair.
quests.funFact: Labeling your snacks can help family members know which treats are saved!

quests.instruction: You get to go swimming for the first time this summer. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: The first splash of summer can make you want to run straight for the water.
quests.explanation: The first swim of summer fills you with eager, splashy energy.
quests.funFact: Swimming uses almost every muscle in your body — no wonder it feels so fun!

quests.instruction: You find your lost toy under the bed. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: Finding something you thought was gone forever feels wonderful.
quests.explanation: Finding a toy you missed brings a big happy smile to your face.
quests.funFact: Our brains give us a little happy boost whenever we find something we lost!

quests.instruction: The lights suddenly go out during a storm. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Sudden darkness can make your body feel jumpy and unsure.
quests.explanation: Sudden darkness can make your body feel unsure and a little jumpy.
quests.funFact: Keeping a flashlight nearby can help you feel brave during a power outage!

quests.instruction: Your ice cream scoop falls off the cone onto the ground. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Think about your eyes — do they feel a little watery right now?
quests.explanation: Losing a yummy treat you were enjoying can make your eyes feel a little watery.
quests.funFact: It is okay to feel this way about small things — talking about it can help.

quests.instruction: Your sister changes the channel while you are watching your show. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: Losing something you were enjoying because of someone else feels frustrating.
quests.explanation: It is frustrating when someone interrupts something you were enjoying.
quests.funFact: Taking turns with the remote can help everyone feel like it is fair.

quests.instruction: You are going to watch your favorite movie at the theater tonight. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: Waiting for a movie you have wanted to see can make you check the clock a lot.
quests.explanation: Waiting to watch a movie you love can fill you with eager energy.
quests.funFact: The smell of popcorn is part of what makes movie theaters feel so fun!

quests.instruction: Your dad reads you a bedtime story. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: A cozy story before bed can make you feel warm inside.
quests.explanation: Cuddling up for a story with someone who loves you is a happy little moment.
quests.funFact: Bedtime stories can help your brain feel calm and happy before sleep!

quests.instruction: A big dog barks loudly right next to you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Loud, sudden barks close by can make you want to step back.
quests.explanation: Loud, sudden barking close to you can make your body want to jump back.
quests.funFact: Most dogs bark just to say hello — staying calm can help you feel braver.

quests.instruction: You miss the school bus in the morning. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Watching the bus drive away without you might make your shoulders slump.
quests.explanation: Missing something you were counting on can leave you with a heavy, quiet feeling.
quests.funFact: A few slow, deep breaths can help your body feel calmer after a rushed morning.

quests.instruction: Your little brother knocks down the tower you built. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: When your hard work gets ruined, your hands might make tight fists.
quests.explanation: Having something you built get knocked down can make you feel hot and cross.
quests.funFact: Taking slow, deep breaths can help your body cool down when this happens.

quests.instruction: You find out you are getting a new puppy tomorrow. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: Waiting for a brand new furry friend can make the day feel extra long.
quests.explanation: Waiting for a brand-new furry friend fills you with eager, joyful energy.
quests.funFact: Puppies usually leave their mothers around 8 weeks old to join their new families!

quests.instruction: You get a new puppy to play with. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: A brand new furry friend to play with feels wonderful.
quests.explanation: A brand-new puppy to love and play with brings lots of happiness.
quests.funFact: Puppies wag their tails when they feel happy too, just like you smile!

quests.instruction: You have to walk into a dark room alone to grab something. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Stepping into the dark alone can make your heart beat a little quicker.
quests.explanation: Stepping into the dark by yourself can make your heart beat a bit faster.
quests.funFact: Humming a favorite tune can help you feel braver when walking through the dark!

quests.instruction: Your friend cannot come to your birthday party. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Missing a friend on a special day can bring a small frown.
quests.explanation: Missing someone on a day you were looking forward to can feel disappointing.
quests.funFact: You can save a slice of cake or send a photo to share the fun with them later!

quests.instruction: Someone pops your balloon on purpose. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: When someone breaks your fun on purpose, your eyebrows might scrunch down.
quests.explanation: When someone ruins your fun on purpose, it is normal to feel upset and cross.
quests.funFact: Telling a grown-up when someone breaks the rules on purpose can help fix things.

quests.instruction: Your team is about to play in the championship game. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: A big, important game can make your heart pump with eager energy.
quests.explanation: Playing in a big, important game fills your body with eager, ready energy.
quests.funFact: Athletes often do a little warm-up dance to use this bouncy energy before a big game!

quests.instruction: Your friend shares candy with you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: When a friend is kind and shares, your smile grows big.
quests.explanation: Sharing and kindness from a friend make you smile with happiness.
quests.funFact: Sharing makes both friends feel good — the one who shares and the one who receives!

quests.instruction: You see a big, moving shadow on your bedroom wall. How do you feel?
quests.question: Scared
quests.hint: Strange shapes in the dark can make your tummy feel fluttery.
quests.explanation: Strange shadows in a dim room can give you a fluttery, unsure feeling.
quests.funFact: Turning on a light often shows a spooky shadow is just a coat or a chair!

quests.instruction: You cannot find your teddy bear at bedtime. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Not finding a comfy friend at bedtime can make your lip curl down.
quests.explanation: Missing a cozy bedtime friend can bring on a quiet, teary feeling.
quests.funFact: Looking together with a grown-up can help you find lost things and feel better fast!

quests.instruction: Your friend will not share the swing even after you asked nicely. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: Waiting a long time for a turn that never comes can feel very unfair.
quests.explanation: Waiting a long time without getting a fair turn can feel really frustrating.
quests.funFact: Setting a turn-timer can help friends share the swing fairly!

quests.instruction: You are on your way to the amusement park. How do you feel?
quests.question: Excited
quests.hint: Thinking about rides and games waiting for you can make you bounce in your seat.
quests.explanation: Heading somewhere full of fun rides and games fills you with bouncy energy.
quests.funFact: Roller coasters were first built over 100 years ago and people still love them!

quests.instruction: Your team scores a goal. How do you feel?
quests.question: Happy
quests.hint: Cheering and clapping happen when something great happens in a game.
quests.explanation: Scoring a goal with your team is a moment to cheer and feel happy.
quests.funFact: Celebrating together as a team can make happy feelings even bigger!
